liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (3 reviews): Kesey recites a poem and ad libs while the band plays intensely behind him after Dark Star; The band follows Kesey's rant closely, which the reviewer calls one of the most powerful moments [17][23][24]
- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Ken Kesey's rap comes during the jam inside Dark Star; The reviewer says Dark Star alone justifies listening to the show [14][15]
- **Throwin' Stones** (1 review): The reviewer calls the Throwin' Stones jam insane and their favorite jam of the concert [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Werewolves of London**: back after 466 archived shows (2191 days); rare: 12 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd91-10-31.sbd.gardner.2897.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 177 min; rated 4.89/5 by 56 [1]. Said about its sound: This soundboard copy is clean and complete; an earlier copy the reviewer had contained a few drops; The recording sounds good, but the reviewer says the live experience was far better [14][15]
- **gd1991-10-31.sbd.hinko.32241.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 180 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Uploader notes no dropout in Let It Grow, and discs 2 and 3 join seamlessly [4]
- **gd1991-10-31.mtx.haugh.gems.102251.flac24**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1991-10-31.mtx.haugh.gems.102252.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 177 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [3]

## Around the show

- Gary Duncan sat in as a guest and added extra energy to the show [14]
- Kesey's brief performance made it the spookiest Halloween the reviewer had seen; mood was heightened by Bill Graham's recent passing [15]
- Reviewer stood near the stage on Phil's side in the Coliseum stands; the parking lot was wild with costumes [16]
- Tickets were nearly impossible to get unless you already had one [16]
- The second set has many small haunting moments fitting for Halloween [17]
- The review quotes an E. E. Cummings poem about Buffalo Bill, which echoes the Halloween, death-themed mood [18]
- Kesey acts as a shaman in the second set, which feels intense and creepy [19]
- Kesey's rap chilled the crowd, and the mood was different because people sensed an era ending with Bill's passing [22]
- The reviewer says October 26, 1989 has a similar eerie vibe [19]
- Some regard it as part of the last great run of shows, played under sad circumstances [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-10-31.sbd.gardner.2897.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The reviewer had lost their own tape of the show eight years earlier [21]
- **gd1991-10-31.sbd.hinko.32241.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by eD; source: DSBD > DAT > CD > EAC > FLAC [4]. Also: Extracted with EAC in secure mode, joined and checked with SHNtool, edited in Cool Edit Pro, encoded to FLAC [4]
- **gd1991-10-31.mtx.haugh.gems.102251.flac24**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD+AUD Matrix Mix (60% SBD & 40% AUD) Multitrack Mixdown: SBD -3db, Aud -8db [2]
- **gd1991-10-31.mtx.haugh.gems.102252.flac16**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD+AUD Matrix Mix (60% SBD & 40% AUD); Multitrack Mixdown: SBD -3db, Aud -8db; Matrix by Amdig [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - October 31, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/october-31-1991) [31]
